fields.meta_description: Build an affidavit form that asks for each fact, fills a PDF ready for the notary and keeps every sworn statement in a table you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Affidavit Form Signers Fill Before the Notary
fields.hero_description: Describe the statement to be sworn. Emergent builds the affidavit form, turns each answer into a numbered paragraph and saves every finished affidavit in a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: A sworn statement holds up when each part is where a court or notary expects it. These six features put every part in place.
fields.feature_1:
Each fact in its own paragraph

Emergent asks one question per fact and writes every answer as a numbered paragraph in the first person. The affiant reads the whole statement back before they submit it.
fields.feature_2:
Venue and affiant at the top

State and county lines head the document, then the affiant's full name and home address. Collect them once and they also fill the closing signature block and the notary's lines.
fields.feature_3:
A filled PDF for the notary

Submitting the form fills the affidavit and renders it as a PDF with an empty signature line and a notary block. The affiant prints it and signs only with the notary watching.
fields.feature_4:
Exhibits attached and lettered

Receipts and photos upload with the answers. Each file gets a letter in the order the statement mentions it, and the files are attached behind the last page of the PDF.
fields.feature_5:
Every affidavit in one table

Each submission becomes a row with the affiant, the matter, the date drafted and whether it has been notarized. Filter by matter, or open any row to download its PDF again.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your source code

Publish the form on your own domain or share it as a private link. Export the full source to GitHub whenever a developer wants to add case numbers or a client portal.
fields.why_description: A blank court PDF leaves the affiant to work out the wording alone, and each finished copy ends up in a folder nobody searches.

fields.usecase_heading: Affidavit Forms for Every Sworn Statement
fields.tab_content_1:
Client answers turn into numbered paragraphs

A paralegal at Harlow Legal sends a client one link for a witness affidavit in a fence dispute. The client answers eight questions about what they saw, and each answer becomes a numbered paragraph. The attorney flags paragraph 6 for a date the client guessed at. The PDF reaches the client for signing only after that fix.
fields.tab_content_2:
Notary appointments start from a filled PDF

Signers book a mobile notary and complete their general affidavit on the same form, typing the statement under their name and address. The notary gets each filled PDF the evening before. The 2:30 pm signer brings photo ID and signs with the notary present, with nothing left to write by hand.
fields.tab_content_3:
Enrollment waits for the host family's statement

Parents moving in with relatives fill an affidavit of residency, and the homeowner adds a statement through a second link. The registrar sees every file in one table. Any file missing the host's statement or a utility bill is held, and the parent gets an email. Three of this week's 41 files are on hold.
fields.tab_content_4:
Council members file before any vote

In Texas, a council member with a substantial interest in a business on the agenda files an affidavit stating the nature and extent of that interest before the vote. The form asks for the business, the interest and the agenda item. The city secretary gets the signed PDF, and item 7 shows the member as abstaining.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Affidavit Form
fields.howto_description: Settle the facts and the oath before you build a single field.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what you saw or did
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the venue at the top
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write each fact on its own line, with the date and the place it happened. Every line becomes a question on the form and a numbered paragraph in the finished affidavit. Ten short facts read better than three long ones.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the state and county where the affiant will swear to the statement. If the affidavit supports a court case, add the court name and case number exactly as they appear on the earlier filings.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Phrase each question so the answer is a plain statement: what happened, when and where. Ask how the affiant knows it, too. A neighbor who watched the fence fall writes a stronger paragraph than one who heard about it later.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the affidavit in a sentence or two and paste in the oath wording your court or notary uses. Emergent builds the questions and the PDF, and stores each submission in a table. Change any of it later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Choose a notary or a declaration
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide how the statement gets sworn. Most affidavits are signed before a notary, who completes the jurat at the bottom. If your filing accepts a declaration under penalty of perjury instead, build a second version of the PDF without the notary block.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose who reads every statement before the PDF goes out. A law firm might send each draft to the supervising attorney, while a notary office might only confirm the venue and name fields. Reviewers get an email with a link to the draft.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with a made-up affiant
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form as a fictional affiant, attach a test exhibit and read the PDF line by line. Check that paragraph numbers run in order and each exhibit letter matches the text. Have an attorney read the template wording before anyone signs a real one.

claims_to_source: An affidavit is a written statement of facts the affiant personally knows, sworn to be true and usually signed in front of someone authorized to take oaths, such as a notary public; a false statement in it is perjury
If the signature needs a notary, the affiant does not sign until in front of the notary; legal aid sites publish free blank affidavit PDFs
A jurat is the notarial act in which the signer swears or affirms that the contents of the document are true
An affidavit used in federal summary judgment must be made on personal knowledge, set out facts that would be admissible in evidence and show the affiant is competent to testify
Under 28 U.S.C. 1746, an unsworn declaration signed under penalty of perjury can stand in for an affidavit in most federal matters

In Texas, a local public official with a substantial interest in a business entity or real property files an affidavit stating the nature and extent of the interest with the official record keeper before a vote, and abstains from further participation
